title: A monitor alarm sounds: patient first
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
Only the patient-first principle is written.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Put the patient before the machine when an alarm sounds.

sources.use: Open RN Advanced Skills 7.4: assess the patient first when the ECG changes

setup: A fictional monitored adult on a fictional unit; the monitor shows a new abnormal rhythm.

options.text: Go to the patient immediately, assess responsiveness, breathing, pulse and perfusion, and activate the appropriate urgent or arrest response if indicated.
options.feedback: Assess the patient rather than treating the monitor tracing alone. Do not delay emergency help or CPR when arrest is suspected while checking the equipment.

options.text: Silence the alarm and look at the printout later.
Change the monitor settings to stop the alarm.
options.feedback: Alarm settings follow order or policy.
